title: Managing boarding facilities during the long holiday
description: A practical guide for Kenyan boarding school principals on securing, maintaining, and preparing facilities during the extended holiday period between terms.
body:
The long holiday between academic years is the best window a boarding school has for major maintenance, security review, and facility preparation — but only if this time is used deliberately. Facilities left unattended for weeks without a clear plan are facilities that deteriorate, and security gaps during an empty holiday period create genuine risk.

Security during the holiday period

An empty boarding school compound is a specific security consideration — theft of equipment, unauthorised access, vandalism all become more likely without visible, consistent oversight. A clear holiday security arrangement, whether through retained staff, a contracted security service, or a rotation of responsible personnel, should be confirmed and documented before the holiday begins, not arranged informally at the last minute.

Using the holiday window for maintenance

Maintenance priorities during the break

  • Repairs that cannot be done while dormitories are occupied — electrical work, plumbing, structural repairs
  • Deep cleaning of dormitories, kitchens, and dining facilities
  • Pest control treatments that require the space to be vacated
  • Painting, roofing, or other works disruptive to daily boarding life

Planning tip: Compile a maintenance priority list during the term, as issues are noticed, rather than trying to remember or identify them all at the start of the holiday. A running list maintained by the bursar or facilities staff throughout the term makes holiday planning far more efficient.

Kitchen and food storage management

Unused kitchen facilities and food storage over an extended holiday carry specific risks — spoilage, pest infestation, equipment left in a state that creates problems at the start of next term. A clear handover process, with a designated staff member responsible for kitchen wind-down and pre-term readiness, prevents the first week of next term being consumed by kitchen setup problems.

Water and electricity systems

Water tanks, electrical systems, and any standby generators benefit from being checked and serviced during the holiday period, rather than discovering a fault only when the school reopens and demand returns. A brief system check a week or two before reopening, rather than on the day students return, allows time to address any issues found.

Preparing for reopening

A facilities readiness check — conducted a few days before students and staff return, covering dormitories, water, electricity, kitchen, and classrooms — confirms the compound is genuinely ready rather than assuming it is because the holiday has simply ended. This check should be documented so facility staff and the principal have a clear record of what was confirmed.
